plan.question: Can stage 1 of the Sinkhorn redo (refit of the 180 A1 Sinkhorn rows with the corrected Sinkhorn code, SI-51/SI-57) be launched from a clean checkout of tag prereg-tier12-v3, and what will it cost?
plan.primary_outcome: Stage 1 launch gate (no scientific outcome is computed here): 180 of 180 rows reach a final state (scored, diverged or nonfinite_latent) with one scorer provenance, run_stage completion gate exit 0. The registered primary outcome of the downstream analysis (R1, noise-calibrated batch and bio scores, PREREG section 2) is unchanged and is not touched.
plan.unit_of_analysis: one A1 Sinkhorn fit = one manifest row (task, decoder condition, penalty strength, seed)
plan.split_unit: not applicable: no held-out split is created or used by stage 1 (all cells are used for fitting; train_size 0.9 is the registered scVI validation split inside the fitter)
plan.selection_rule: none at this stage: the 180 rows are fixed by manifests/paper_manifest_stock_pilot_u5_b10_v3.tsv; the penalty strength is selected later by R1 (rule order, SI-57), not here
plan.multiple_comparison_correction: not applicable: one gate decision (launch / do not launch); no hypothesis test or ranking is made by stage 1
plan.data_filters: rows with experiment == A1 and arm == sinkhorn (tasks atac_small, immune, sim1; both decoder conditions; seeds 100-102; 10 penalty strengths); no cell filtering

extra_items.question: Are any evaluated labels constant within a donor/patient (donor-level), and if so is the train/test split grouped by donor rather than by cell?
extra_items.applies_if: A probe, classifier or held-out metric uses labels such as response, treatment time, disease, genotype or any per-sample/per-patient annotation.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_donor_split(adata, label_cols, donor_col, split_col=...) on the realized split; a label with one value per donor is donor-level and needs a donor-grouped split.

extra_items.question: Is the grouping key unique across cohorts (composite cohort.patient), with the sample-to-patient mapping verified rather than assumed?
extra_items.applies_if: Data from more than one cohort/study/assay is pooled, or the grouping column is a sample/batch id that is assumed to equal one patient.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_donor_split(..., cohort_col=..., sample_col=...) and inspect id collisions and sample-to-donor nesting; check prior notes/memory for recorded collisions before writing guidance.

extra_items.question: On the realized train/test assignment, does any donor/group appear on both sides?
extra_items.applies_if: Any train/test, held-out or cross-validation split exists for data with repeated cells per donor/sample.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_split_leakage(adata, group_col, split_col) on the saved split labels, not on the splitting code.

extra_items.question: Are guarantees claimed for a custom grouped-split function (no straddling, target fraction, optimality) verified empirically over many seeds?
extra_items.applies_if: A custom grouped/stratified split function is written or its docstring states a guarantee.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_split_fn(split_fn, group_ids, n_seeds=10, check_optimal=True) and compare reported side stability and optimality gap with the docstring.

extra_items.question: Does every feature in the gene panel / program gene set belong to the intended species (ENSG vs ENSMUSG, symbol case)?
extra_items.applies_if: A gene panel, feature set or program gene set is built from a reference or dataset that may combine species, or a dataset's species is assumed from its name.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_species(adata_or_var_names, expected='human') on the final panel, the program gene set and each model input.

extra_items.question: Does each model's required gene vocabulary cover the dataset's genes, and are models with incompatible species/ID types excluded or reported on the compatible subset?
extra_items.applies_if: A foundation model with a fixed gene vocabulary (token dictionary, species-specific ID list) is evaluated.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_vocab_coverage(var_names, vocab, min_frac=...) per model x dataset; list which datasets each model is excluded from and why.

extra_items.question: Is the zero-intensity perturbation exactly the raw input (a true no-op), for every dataset and every perturbation type, including default dispersion/shape parameters?
extra_items.applies_if: A perturbation axis (noise, dropout, variance shift, batch effect, etc.) includes a level that is meant to be the unperturbed baseline.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_noop_perturbation(raw, perturbed_at_zero) per dataset; any nonzero difference or changed shape blocks the run.

extra_items.question: Are cell counts (and per-cell QC statistics) reported along each perturbation axis, and does the retained sample size stay within a stated ratio?
extra_items.applies_if: A perturbation or filtering step varies in severity and downstream metrics are compared across its levels.
extra_items.how_to_check: Tabulate n_cells (and median genes/cell) per dataset x level and run scpf_check_cell_counts(table, axis_col, max_ratio=...).

extra_items.question: Can the perturbation generator produce empty cells or genes, and is that guarded before the model runners see the data?
extra_items.applies_if: Dropout, thinning, subsampling or count-level noise is applied before model fitting.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_empty_cells(perturbed, min_genes=1) over the full perturbation grid, not one setting.

extra_items.question: Do the number of genes reaching each model match the declared panel size, and is HVG selection a real ranking (n_top_genes < n_vars) applied exactly once?
extra_items.applies_if: HVG selection or a fixed gene-panel size is configured and results are compared across models or datasets.
extra_items.how_to_check: Record n_genes at model input per model x dataset and run scpf_check_gene_counts(n_genes_by_model, expected_n, hvg_n, n_vars_input, n_hvg_stages).

extra_items.question: Are batch key, condition and donor columns resolved by explicit name and validated by expected values, never by column position or a heuristic first match?
extra_items.applies_if: A script, smoke test or loader selects obs/metadata columns (batch_key, condition, donor, label).
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_obs_keys(adata, required={role: column}, expected_values=..., used={role: resolved column}) in the loader and the smoke test.

extra_items.question: Does the claimed finding (e.g. batch demoted below biology) go beyond what the model's batch/covariate conditioning mechanism does by construction?
extra_items.applies_if: A claim of disentanglement, invariance or integration is made for a model whose decoder or encoder is explicitly conditioned on the covariate in question.
extra_items.how_to_check: List each model's conditioning inputs from its source; label such results as conditioning/integration effects, and require an unconditioned comparison or ablation before claiming disentanglement.

extra_items.question: Are factor pairs deterministically nested (one factor fully determines the other) and excluded from collision/overlap counts and dependence metrics?
extra_items.applies_if: Several covariates (batch, response, time, cancer type, donor) are scored against each other or against latent dimensions.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_nesting(adata, factors, pairs=...) and drop or separately report nested pairs.

extra_items.question: Is each model scored in its native concept basis (block metrics for block-structured latents, per-dimension only for one-dimension-per-factor), and are block-sensitive probes and reproducibility scores valid for residual blocks?
extra_items.applies_if: Models with multi-dimensional concept blocks (shared/private/residual subspaces) are compared with per-dimension disentanglement metrics (MIG, DCI, SAP, completeness).
extra_items.how_to_check: Build layouts from each model's source (None if no block structure) and run scpf_check_block_scoring(layouts, bases); fail on silent fallback to per-dimension.

extra_items.question: Is block-to-factor pairing an explicit name map, with unowned/shared blocks not credited to any factor?
extra_items.applies_if: A block-aware metric pairs latent blocks with annotated factors.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_block_pairing(blocks, factors, pairing, shared_blocks).

extra_items.question: Are kNN-based metric parameters valid for the smallest sample at every condition (trustworthiness k < n/2; kNN k < n; kBET k <= n)?
extra_items.applies_if: A kNN-derived metric (trustworthiness, kNN purity/NMI, kBET, LISI) is computed on subsampled, filtered or perturbed data of varying size.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_knn_validity(n_cells_by_condition, k, kind) before computing; ensure invalid cells are NaN with a status string.

extra_items.question: Are non-computable metric cells reported as NaN with a status string (never a placeholder value), and are NaN columns traced to their true cause?
extra_items.applies_if: Any metric can be undefined for some dataset/model/condition.
extra_items.how_to_check: Scan result tables for constants such as 1.0000/0.0 on infeasible cells; confirm each NaN has a status and the cause is read from the code path, not guessed.

extra_items.question: Do all pooled models cover the same datasets; if not, is pooling restricted to the common subset (or coverage shown) and rank stability checked?
extra_items.applies_if: Metrics are averaged across datasets per model and some models run on a subset (species restriction, memory, failed fits).
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_pool_coverage(table, model_col, dataset_col, value_col); report coverage next to every pooled figure.

extra_items.question: Do results loaders reject retired/stale perturbation types and result files by their value, not only by a missing field?
extra_items.applies_if: Result JSON/CSV files from earlier code versions can exist in the same directory as current outputs.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_check_allowed_values(pert_types_in_files, allowed, name='perturbation type') over every loaded file; confirm baseline slices contain only current-run files.

extra_items.question: Did any runner catch an exception and continue with a different method (e.g. refit on all cells instead of held-out projection, retry-then-ignore)?
extra_items.applies_if: Model runners wrap fits/projections in try/except, retry-then-ignore, or version-sensitive library calls.
extra_items.how_to_check: Run scpf_scan_fallbacks(log_text_or_path) on all runner logs and grep runner code for broad excepts around projection/transform; confirm every expected cell of the result grid exists.

extra_items.question: Are continuous factors (program scores, pseudotime, dose) kept as ordered axes, not binned into unordered classes for classifier-based metrics?
extra_items.applies_if: A classifier- or MI-based disentanglement metric is applied to a continuous factor.
extra_items.how_to_check: Confirm the metric variant used for continuous factors is regression/ordered; document any binning and its justification.

extra_items.question: Is every statement that a metric is standard in single-cell benchmarking backed by a cited single-cell source?
extra_items.applies_if: A metric suite is justified by field convention in a plan, README or manuscript.
extra_items.how_to_check: Find a single-cell benchmark paper using the metric (open the full text); otherwise word it as borrowed from general ML disentanglement.
